findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Covered container of cheese sauce (product thicker than 4 inches) prepared that morning was observed in an ice bath on the kitchen counter. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 106F and 140F respectively. Cook stated preparation of the cheese sauce began around 11a, but the product not labeled to indicate the time when cooling process began. Cheese sauce was separated into two containers on an ice bath, and internal temperatures were observed to be below 70F for one container and around 100F for the other after 1hr. Proper cooling and labeling of cooked, cooling foods were discussed.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.
Cooked PHF shall be cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. The only way to accurately know the temperature of cooling foods is to use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to check the temperature during the cooling process. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods and the time to ensure they are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling. Separate foods into smaller portions and place on ice baths (stirring frequently) to help rapidly drop the temperature of cooling foods. Also, it is ok to leave cooling foods uncovered during the cooling process and then cover them tightly once the cooling process has been completed..

findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Boxes of potato chips were stored near kitchen handsink on a small plastic rack. Sides of boxes were getting splashed when handsink was used, and the bottom box was less than 6 inches off the floor. Boxes of chips were moved to shelves in the dry storage area. Foods shall be protected at all times. Store foods at least 6 inches off the floor. B) Open container of pineapple juice was observed in bar cooler. Bartender and kitchen manager were advised on proper storage of acidic foods once original cans are opened. Pineapple juice was placed in a pitcher for storage. Do not store acidic products in original cans once they are opened. Metals/metallic flavors can leak into the foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Soiled parchment paper was observed lining backing sheets used for storage. Remove and discard soiled parchment paper. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Bar 3 part sink was setup improperly in the order of wash, sanitize, rinse. Ware washing had not yet occurred. Bartender was advised on proper setup for manual ware washing. Sinks with sanitizer and rinse water were empted and 3 part sink was setup in proper order. Manual ware washing handout provided for staff. Maintain 3 part sink in the order of wash, rinse, and sanitize during manual ware washing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was observed sitting at the corner of the bar counter. Bartender noted the cloth was dipped in the sanitizer solution in the 3 part sink prior to use. Bartender was advised to maintain a bucket of sanitizer solution separate from 3 part sink and store the wiping cloth in the solution between uses. Change solution every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) inside microwave; B) (R) trays of small pizza ovens; C) spouts of bulk ketchup & mustard dispensers; D) cooking lid under flat grill; E) can opener blade; & F) bar soda gun - buildup around area where nozzle attaches and in the bottom of the holder. Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) bottom inside pot/pan storage (food debris); B) counter under popcorn machine at bar; C) tracks of all sliding door coolers; D) tray under flat grill with cleaning equipment; E) bin under red cutting board at banquet room bar; F) black fan in  banquet room bar; G) backing sheet & bucket full of grease below kitchen 3 part sink; H) black cart with slushie machine; & I) electrical base of cheese sauce warmer. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Storage area for grill utensils and clean bowls and plates was soiled with crumbs and splash. One bowl had crumbs in the bottom. Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Maintain storage areas for cleaned/sanitized equipment clean so items are protected from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Leak was observed near the lever of the water line connected to the dish machine. Maintenance worker observed the area of concern and noted part of the line probably needs to be replaced. Proper repairs will be made as soon as possible. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Men's room at far end of hallway had missing/loose baseboard in a few areas. Other men's room had loose baseboard at the corner behind the toilet. B) Baseboard was loose along the top at the far left corner below bulk ketchup & mustard dispensers. C) Baseboard behind water line of dish machine had a hole in it. Repair/replace baseboard in the aforementioned areas. D) Floors were soiled under the beef storage shelf in walkin freezer, in alcohol walkin cooler, and behind the dish machine. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.
